items.text: Explain the three pillars of IAM: Authentication, Authorization, Audibility
Name the four IAM principal types and the key difference between a group and a role
Explain why the root user must be locked away after initial setup
Name the 9 AWS services that support resource-based policies
Recite the three-step IAM evaluation rule from memory
Explain the difference between MultiFactorAuthPresent and MultiFactorAuthAge
Read any IAM policy JSON and identify Effect, Action, Resource, Condition
Grade a policy as Narrow, Medium, or Wide on both the action and resource axes
Identify whether a policy is identity-based or resource-based from the JSON
Construct the correct ARN format for S3 (no region, no account-id)
Trace a complete cross-account access flow from EC2 in Account B to S3 in Account A
Identify the four places to check when a cross-account KMS+S3 call fails with Access Denied
Design an IAM architecture that satisfies: no deletion, fresh MFA, permission boundaries for developers
Eliminate wildcard-action or wildcard-resource answers as least-privilege violations
Apply the explicit deny rule instantly: deny wins over allow in all policy types
Distinguish source account from destination account in cross-account scenarios
Choose MultiFactorAuthAge (not Present) for session-hijacking defense questions
Recognize the KMS two-pronged rule: both IAM role policy AND KMS key policy must allow kms:Decrypt
